newsitem.title: ITALY: Cariplo wants tie with Ambroveneto.
newsitem.headline: Cariplo wants tie with Ambroveneto.

text.p: Italian savings bank Cariplo is to seek a strategic link-up with Banco Ambrosiano Veneto which could involve Ambroveneto acquiring shares in Cariplo, Milan daily Il Sole 24 ore said on Tuesday.

The executive body of the Cariplo foundation, which owns Cariplo, took the decision to formally approach Ambroveneto at a meeting on Monday chaired by its new president Giuseppe Guzzetti, the newspaper reported.

Guzzetti said last week that the bank would start a process of privatisation in 1997 and that it was aiming to establish a strategic partnership, possibly with an Italian bank which included foreign institutions among its shareholders.
Il Sole said the Cariplo foundation would offer Ambroveneto the option of subscribing to shares in the savings bank, Cariplo Spa, when it is floated on the stock exchange.

Ambroveneto chairman Giovanni Bazoli will have to convince the main partners in a shareholders' syndicate which controls Ambroveneto to subscribe to a capital increase to raise enough funds to acquire Cariplo stock, the newspaper said.
The main shareholder in the syndicate is Credit Agricole, with 29 percent of Ambroveneto, which is believed to be interested in subscribing to the capital increase, the newspaper said.

Other shareholders, including Cassa di Risparmio di Verona, with 12.7 percent, and insurance group Alleanza, with 16 percent, are thought to have misgivings about putting up more cash, it added. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
